combined_title: From Passive Prompts to Active Agents: Transforming Campus Workflows with M-Connectors
description:
Move beyond static prompt-and-response AI. This hands-on workshop introduces M-Connectors—a Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration that connects U-M GPT directly to live campus systems, external APIs, and active data repositories. Discover how to transform GenAI into active agents capable of querying live data, maintaining deep context, and performing authorized tasks across tools like Canvas, Google Workspace, Slack, and Zoom—all within U-M's secure enterprise privacy boundary.

What You'll Learn

--The MCP Advantage: How M-Connectors query live campus systems without custom code while preserving U-M enterprise data security.
--Instructor Workflows: Automate Canvas readiness checks, synthesize lecture transcripts into study guides, generate 4-tier rubrics, and draft personalized student reminders based on live gradebook data.
--Administrative Workflows: Extract insights from Google Forms/Sheets, summarize Zoom meetings and Slack threads into action items, and query active Drive folders to draft communications.
--The 15 Launch Connectors: Explore core connector capabilities across U-M GPT and Maizey to build your own custom productivity workflows.

combined_title: Kathy Beck & Vinson Lam, carillon
description:
Kathy Beck & Vinson Lam perform on the Charles Baird Carillon, an instrument of 53 bronze bells located inside the Burton Memorial Tower. The largest bell, which strikes the hour, weighs 12 tons, while the smallest bell, 4½ octaves above, weighs just 15 pounds.

Thirty-minute recitals are performed on the Charles Baird Carillon at noon every weekday that classes are in session, followed by visitor Q&A with the carillonist. The bell chamber may be accessed via a combination of elevator and stairs. Take the elevator to the highest floor possible (floor 8), and then climb two flights of stairs (39 steps) to the bell chamber (floor 10). Hearing protection earmuffs are provided for visitors. Be prepared to walk on ice and snow in the bell chamber during winter. Built in 1936, the Charles Baird Carillon is not ADA accessible. Visitors with mobility concerns are invited to visit the Lurie Carillon.

event_title: LRCCS Noon Lecture Series | From a 'Ton of Steel' to 'Another Province Overseas': Foreign and Diaspora Tourism to Mao-Era China
combined_title: LRCCS Noon Lecture Series | From a 'Ton of Steel' to 'Another Province Overseas': Foreign and Diaspora Tourism to Mao-Era China: Gavin Healy, Columbia University
description:
Please note: This lecture will be held in person and virtually on Zoom. If you would like to attend via Zoom, registration is required. Once you've registered, joining information will be sent to your email. Register for the Zoom webinar at: https://myumi.ch/gk19J

In the early years of the People’s Republic of China, state tourism officials saw sightseeing as a form of public diplomacy, but noted also that they could earn as much from hosting just one Soviet tourist as they could from exporting a ton of steel. At the same time, the vast majority of visitors to China during the Mao years came from China’s diaspora, which officials referred to as “another province overseas” that could contribute to the economic and political foundations of the new nation. This talk will examine the challenges faced by China’s state tourism officials in promoting foreign and diaspora tourism as a form of public diplomacy and economic development from the founding of the PRC to the Cultural Revolution.

Gavin Healy is a center associate of the Lieberthal-Rogel Center for Chinese Studies at the University of Michigan and has taught Chinese history at Columbia University and the State University of New York. He is the author of *A Guide to Mao’s China: Showing the Nation to Foreign Guests* (Cornell University Press, 2026). His work appears in *20th Century China*, *Modern China*, and the *Journal of Contemporary History*.
